The lobed, pale gland opening into the hair follicle is a sebaceous (oil) gland.

stem: If you pricked your fingertip with a needle, the first layer of the epidermis that it would penetrate is the:
explanation: The stratum corneum is the outermost layer, so it is the first layer anything touches.

stem: What layer of skin is present in thick skin but NOT in thin skin?
explanation: The stratum lucidum is a clear layer found only in thick skin (palms and soles).

stem: Thick skin contains more layers than thin skin.
explanation: Thick skin has five epidermal layers; thin skin lacks the stratum lucidum, so it has four.

stem: What layer of the epidermis do we shed on a daily basis?
explanation: Dead cells of the stratum corneum flake off continuously and are replaced from below.

stem: What layer of skin acts as a water-repellent?
explanation: Cells of the stratum granulosum release lipids that waterproof the skin.

stem: What is the portion called that surrounds the hair root?
explanation: The hair follicle is the sheath of epithelium and connective tissue that surrounds the hair root.
